chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performs the ritual bath for pilgrimage (ziarah) and then sleeps; does he perform ablution before visiting? He said, 'He must repeat his ritual bath, because he only entered [the state of ritual purity] with ablution.'
And similarly, it is recommended for a woman to perform the ritual bath before she performs the circumambulation (tawaf). Narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ritual purity if one sleeps after performing ghusl for pilgrimage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the major bath (ghusl) for ziyarah is primarily intended to confer the state of minor ablution (wudu); thus, if one sleeps and breaks their wudu, the original ghusl is considered insufficient for the act of worship, necessitating a renewal. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of a specific ritual bath depends on its intended purpose and the preservation of the accompanying minor purity state. The extension to women performing tawaf underscores the universal application of these purity conditions for entering the sacred precincts of the Kaaba.
